\section[l'ostacolo]{l'ostacolo — the obstacle}

\label{lesson:IT-C354-ostacolo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the excuse, then the Italian for to justify.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'ostacolo}
\textbf{l'ostacolo} — \textquotedblleft{}the obstacle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La lingua è il primo ostacolo per chi arriva in un paese nuovo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Language is the first obstacle for someone arriving in a new country.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Superare un ostacolo} — to overcome an obstacle. In sport, \emph{i 110 ostacoli} are the hurdles.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ostacolo} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{obstāculum} \textquotedblleft{}a hindrance\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{obstāre} \textquotedblleft{}to stand in the way\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{ob} \textquotedblleft{}against\textquotedblright{} and \emph{stāre} \textquotedblleft{}to stand\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'ostacolo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'ostacolo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'ostacolo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the excuse, then the Italian for to justify, then say \emph{l'ostacolo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does l'ostacolo mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The obstacle\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ostacolare]{ostacolare — to hinder, to obstruct}

\label{lesson:IT-C354-ostacolare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to justify, then the Italian for the obstacle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: ostacolare}
\textbf{ostacolare} — \textquotedblleft{}to hinder, to obstruct\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il traffico ostacola il lavoro delle ambulanze.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The traffic hinders the work of the ambulances.}
\end{quote}

Stress on the second syllable: \emph{ostàcolo}, \emph{ostàcola}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ostacolare} is built on \emph{ostacolo} \textquotedblleft{}obstacle\textquotedblright{}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{obstāculum}, from \emph{obstāre} \textquotedblleft{}to stand in the way\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{stāre} \textquotedblleft{}to stand\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ostacolare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ostacolare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ostacolare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to justify, then the Italian for the obstacle, then say \emph{ostacolare} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[impedire]{impedire — to prevent, to stop (from)}

\label{lesson:IT-C354-impedire}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the obstacle, then the Italian for to hinder.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: impedire}
\textbf{impedire} — \textquotedblleft{}to prevent, to stop (from)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La nebbia ci ha impedito di partire.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The fog prevented us from leaving.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Impedire a qualcuno di fare qualcosa}. Conjugated with \emph{-isc-}: \emph{impedisce}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{impedire} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{impedīre} \textquotedblleft{}to entangle, to hinder\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built from \emph{in} and \emph{pēs, pedis} \textquotedblleft{}foot\textquotedblright{}: to tie someone's feet.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{impedire}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{impedire}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{impedire}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the obstacle, then the Italian for to hinder, then say \emph{impedire} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[favorire]{favorire — to favour, to encourage, to help along}

\label{lesson:IT-C354-favorire}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to hinder, then the Italian for to prevent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: favorire}
\textbf{favorire} — \textquotedblleft{}to favour, to encourage, to help along\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il sole e la pioggia favoriscono la crescita delle piante.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sun and rain help the plants grow.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Favorisca!} — please, help yourself (formal, offering food or a seat).

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{favorire} is built on \emph{favore} \textquotedblleft{}favour\textquotedblright{}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{favor} \textquotedblleft{}goodwill\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{favēre} \textquotedblleft{}to be kind to, to support\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[consentire]{consentire — to allow, to make possible; to consent}

\label{lesson:IT-C354-consentire}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to prevent, then the Italian for to favour.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: consentire}
\textbf{consentire} — \textquotedblleft{}to allow, to make possible; to consent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il nuovo treno consente di arrivare al mare in un'ora.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The new train makes it possible to reach the sea in an hour.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Consentire a qualcuno di fare qualcosa}. Formal next to \emph{permettere}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{consentire} is inherited from Latin \emph{cōnsentīre} \textquotedblleft{}to agree, to feel together\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built from \emph{con-} \textquotedblleft{}together\textquotedblright{} and \emph{sentīre} \textquotedblleft{}to feel\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[(dialogue)]{Ripasso dei capitoli 347–354}

\label{lesson:IT-R354-ripasso-347-354}



\begin{quote}
Say the Italian for to evaluate and the judgement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to evaluate, the judgement, to judge, objective, subjective
  \item the advantage, the disadvantage, the aspect, the criticism, to reiterate
  \item the effect, to bring about, to cause, the factor, the reason
  \item since, given that, so, therefore, due
  \item the origin, to come from, to involve, to determine, to influence
  \item the impact, the repercussion, the implication, to unleash, to trigger
  \item the reaction, to react, the pretext, the excuse, to justify
  \item the obstacle, to hinder, to prevent, to favour, to allow
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To evaluate? (\textbf{valutare}.) The judgement? (\textbf{il giudizio}.) To judge? (\textbf{giudicare}.) Objective? (\textbf{oggettivo}.) Subjective? (\textbf{soggettivo}.) The advantage? (\textbf{il vantaggio}.) The disadvantage? (\textbf{lo svantaggio}.) The aspect? (\textbf{l'aspetto}.) The criticism? (\textbf{la critica}.) To reiterate? (\textbf{ribadire}.) The effect? (\textbf{l'effetto}.) To bring about? (\textbf{provocare}.) To cause? (\textbf{causare}.) The factor? (\textbf{il fattore}.) The reason? (\textbf{la ragione}.) Since? (\textbf{siccome}.) Given that? (\textbf{poiché}.) So? (\textbf{perciò}.) Therefore? (\textbf{pertanto}.) Due? (\textbf{dovuto}.) The origin? (\textbf{l'origine}.) To come from? (\textbf{derivare}.) To involve? (\textbf{comportare}.) To determine? (\textbf{determinare}.) To influence? (\textbf{influire}.) The impact? (\textbf{l'impatto}.) The repercussion? (\textbf{la ripercussione}.) The implication? (\textbf{il risvolto}.) To unleash? (\textbf{scatenare}.) To trigger? (\textbf{innescare}.) The reaction? (\textbf{la reazione}.) To react? (\textbf{reagire}.) The pretext? (\textbf{il pretesto}.) The excuse? (\textbf{la scusa}.) To justify? (\textbf{giustificare}.) The obstacle? (\textbf{l'ostacolo}.) To hinder? (\textbf{ostacolare}.) To prevent? (\textbf{impedire}.) To favour? (\textbf{favorire}.) To allow? (\textbf{consentire}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
